topics.name: Skin & melanoma
topics.overview: Skin cancers include several different diseases. Examination and, when indicated, tissue sampling distinguish them from non-cancerous changes.
symptoms: A new or changing skin lesion
A sore or changing area that does not heal
investigations: Skin examination and dermoscopy
Biopsy with pathology when indicated
treatment: Local removal is used for many skin cancers
Further treatment depends on the confirmed type and extent

topics.name: Mouth & oral cavity
topics.overview: An oral photograph shows visible tissue. A dentist or doctor also examines and feels the mouth and neck; suspicious tissue may need biopsy.
symptoms: A mouth ulcer lasting longer than three weeks
A persistent lump, red or white patch, or swallowing difficulty
investigations: Dental or medical mouth and neck examination
Biopsy and, when needed, imaging for extent
treatment: Surgery or radiotherapy may be considered
Systemic treatment is used in selected circumstances

topics.name: Lung
topics.overview: A CT slice is only part of a lung investigation. Full imaging, clinical history and usually tissue sampling establish the diagnosis and its type.
symptoms: A persistent or changing cough
Breathlessness or coughing up blood
investigations: Clinical assessment and chest imaging
Biopsy and pathology; staging and biomarkers when indicated
treatment: Surgery or radiotherapy in appropriate cases
Systemic treatment selected for the confirmed cancer and biomarkers

topics.name: Breast
topics.overview: Breast findings are assessed with examination, suitable imaging and tissue sampling when needed. An ultrasound classifier does not interpret mammography or MRI.
symptoms: A new breast or armpit lump
Changes in breast skin, shape or nipple
investigations: Breast examination and appropriate imaging
Needle biopsy and pathology when indicated
treatment: Local treatment can include surgery and radiotherapy
Systemic options depend on subtype, stage and other findings

topics.name: Colon & rectum
topics.overview: Bowel changes have many causes. Colorectal assessment can involve examination of the bowel and tissue sampling; a body photograph cannot diagnose it.
symptoms: Blood in the stool
An unexplained change in bowel habits
investigations: Clinical assessment and appropriate bowel tests
Colonoscopy with biopsy when indicated
treatment: Surgery is a common treatment for localized colon cancer
Additional treatment depends on the location, extent and pathology

topics.name: Prostate
topics.overview: Prostate assessment combines history, examination and selected tests. A raised PSA alone does not establish cancer.
symptoms: A change in urine flow
More frequent urination; early disease may have no symptoms
investigations: Discussion of PSA testing and its limitations
Appropriate imaging and biopsy when indicated
treatment: Monitoring can be appropriate for selected cancers
Surgery, radiotherapy or systemic treatment depend on the individual case

topics.name: Cervix
topics.overview: Cervical screening and investigation of symptoms are different tasks. Abnormal findings may require a closer examination and tissue sampling.
symptoms: Unusual vaginal bleeding
An unexplained change in discharge or pelvic symptoms
investigations: Clinical assessment and cervical examination
Colposcopy and biopsy when indicated
treatment: Local treatment or surgery in selected disease
Radiotherapy and systemic treatments according to the confirmed stage

topics.name: Ovary
topics.overview: Persistent abdominal or pelvic symptoms need clinical evaluation. No ordinary photograph or isolated blood marker can confirm ovarian cancer.
symptoms: Persistent abdominal swelling or bloating
Pelvic or abdominal discomfort
investigations: Examination and appropriate pelvic imaging
Blood tests and tissue assessment as directed by the specialist
treatment: Surgery and chemotherapy are common approaches
Other options depend on the exact disease and biomarkers

topics.name: Pancreas
topics.overview: Pancreatic evaluation uses clinical findings and dedicated investigations. Treatment planning depends on extent, operability and the person’s health.
symptoms: Yellowing of the skin or eyes
Persistent upper abdominal or back symptoms
investigations: Clinical assessment, blood tests and dedicated imaging
Endoscopic or tissue assessment when indicated
treatment: Surgery is considered when the disease can be removed
Systemic treatment and supportive care are tailored by the team

topics.name: Liver
topics.overview: Liver cancer assessment depends on clinical history and specialized imaging. The underlying health of the liver also affects treatment choices.
symptoms: Unexplained upper abdominal symptoms
Swelling or yellowing of the skin or eyes
investigations: Liver assessment and appropriate imaging
Additional blood tests or tissue assessment as indicated
treatment: Local procedures, surgery or transplantation in selected cases
Systemic treatment and supportive care when appropriate

topics.name: Kidney
topics.overview: A kidney mass may be found during imaging. Examination and dedicated tests distinguish possible causes and establish the next step.
symptoms: Blood in the urine
An unexplained abdominal lump or persistent side symptoms
investigations: Urine and blood tests with clinical assessment
Dedicated kidney imaging and tissue assessment when indicated
treatment: Surgery or other local approaches in selected cases
Systemic options according to the confirmed disease and extent

topics.name: Brain & central nervous system
topics.overview: Neurological symptoms need clinical assessment. Brain tumors include different diseases; a full scan study and specialist interpretation are essential.
symptoms: New neurological changes
Symptoms vary with the location and type of tumor
investigations: Neurological examination and appropriate MRI or CT
Specialist assessment and tissue diagnosis when feasible
treatment: Surgery or radiotherapy in selected tumors
Other treatment depends on pathology, molecular findings and location

topics.name: Bladder
topics.overview: Blood in the urine has several possible causes and should be assessed. Bladder investigations may include direct inspection and tissue sampling.
symptoms: Blood in the urine
Persistent changes in urination
investigations: Clinical assessment and urine tests
Cystoscopy, tissue sampling and imaging when indicated
treatment: Local procedures or surgery according to disease extent
Bladder-directed or systemic treatment in selected cases

topics.name: Thyroid
topics.overview: A neck or thyroid lump has several possible causes and should be evaluated when persistent. Ultrasound and selected tissue tests guide the assessment.
symptoms: A swelling or lump in the neck
Persistent voice or swallowing changes
investigations: Neck examination and thyroid ultrasound
Needle sampling and other tests when indicated
treatment: Monitoring or surgery in selected situations
Further treatment depends on the specific thyroid cancer

topics.name: Leukaemia · AML reference
topics.overview: Leukaemias are blood-forming tissue cancers with different subtypes. A skin or body photograph cannot establish the diagnosis.
symptoms: Unexplained bruising or bleeding
Persistent fatigue, fever or infections
investigations: Full blood count and blood-film assessment
Bone-marrow and specialist laboratory tests when indicated
treatment: Treatment depends strongly on the leukaemia subtype
Systemic treatment and, in selected cases, stem-cell transplantation

topics.name: Lymphoma · non-Hodgkin reference
topics.overview: Lymphomas are a diverse group of lymph-system cancers. An enlarged lymph node has many possible causes and does not itself establish lymphoma.
symptoms: Persistent enlarged lymph nodes
Unexplained fever, drenching night sweats or weight loss
investigations: History, examination and suitable blood tests
Lymph-node or tissue biopsy and staging investigations
treatment: Observation can be appropriate for some subtypes
Systemic treatment or radiotherapy depends on the exact subtype

faqs.title: How to upload and analyze an image
faqs.text: Choose Skin, Oral, Lung or Breast and select a matching input type. Use Upload an image or drag a JPEG or PNG into the image area. Sign in and confirm the input and local processing permission, then press Run research model. Only installed compatible models can run. Ordinary phone skin photos, mammograms and MRI do not currently have an installed classifier.

faqs.title: What an image-model score means
faqs.text: The digital body is a reference visualization, not a medical scan. An experimental image-model score compares a supplied image with its learned categories. It is not a calibrated personal probability of cancer and cannot confirm or exclude disease. A clinician considers the history, examination, relevant imaging and tests; a biopsy is often needed to establish the diagnosis.

faqs.title: How cancer treatment is chosen
faqs.text: Treatment depends on the confirmed cancer type and extent, relevant biomarkers, overall health and preferences. Options can include surgery, radiotherapy or systemic treatments. This information does not choose a medicine, dose or personal treatment plan. Discuss the appropriate options with the cancer care team.

faqs.title: When not to wait for an AI result
faqs.text: Severe breathing difficulty, heavy bleeding that is not stopping, or coughing up more than a few streaks of blood need emergency care. Even small streaks of coughed-up blood need urgent medical advice. If these describe the current situation, seek medical help rather than waiting for image analysis.
